title: A Gentle Sound May Help the Brain Clean Itself at Night
summary:
During the day, your brain collects waste it no longer needs, including lactic acid and proteins. Sleep gives it a chance to clear those away, as waves of a clear liquid called cerebrospinal fluid move through the brain.

Researchers at MIT found a way to make those fluid waves stronger with bursts of a gentle sound called pink noise. Played at just the right moments during sleep, the sounds boost slow electrical waves in the brain, which produce bigger waves of fluid.

Pink noise sounds softer than white noise, like steady rainfall, and each burst lasted 50 milliseconds.

Timing was everything: each burst had to arrive at the peak of a sleeping person's brain waves.

They tested the idea in 14 healthy volunteers. The timed sounds made the brain waves and the fluid waves bigger, without waking anyone, and scans showed blood vessels pumping fluid out of the brain.

Laura Lewis said the team is excited to try the technology with clinical populations. But the study did not show whether the stronger waves removed more waste or improved sleep quality.
why_it_matters: A good night's sleep helps your brain clean itself, so getting enough sleep helps you think and learn better at school.
